record.original_question: The Hankel matrices of a function f having a Taylor expansion f (z) = a0 + a1 z + . . . are defined by Hp(n) = (aij ); aij = an+1+j−2 ; 1 ≤ i, j ≤ p + 1. (n) If f belongs to the Pick-Nevanlinna class (Det Hp ≥ 0, all n, p), then all the poles of f are simple and they lie on the positive real axis. Denote by (n) (n) ε1 ≥ ε2 ≥ . . . ≥ ε(n) p ≥0 (n) the eigenvalues of Hp . Then (n) 1 lim sup(εj )1/n = , n→∞ λj where λj is the j-th pole, where the poles are numbered in order of increasing modulus. What can be said about the eigenvalues under less restrictive conditions? (R. Bouteiller)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z)=a_0+a_1z+a_2z^2+\cdots$ be a formal power series with complex coefficients. For integers $p\ge 0$ and $n\ge 0$, define the Hankel matrix
$$H_p^{(n)} = (a_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le p+1}, \qquad a_{ij} = a_{n+i+j-2}.$$
Recall that $f$ belongs to the Pick–Nevanlinna class when $\det H_p^{(n)}\ge 0$ for every $n\ge 0$ and every $p\ge 0$. It is known that if $f$ is in the Pick–Nevanlinna class, then all poles of $f$ are simple and lie on the positive real axis; moreover, denoting by
$$\varepsilon_1^{(n)}\ge \varepsilon_2^{(n)}\ge \cdots \ge \varepsilon_{p+1}^{(n)}\ge 0$$
the eigenvalues of $H_p^{(n)}$, one has
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\varepsilon_j^{(n)}\bigr)^{1/n} = \frac{1}{\lambda_j},$$
where $\lambda_1\le \lambda_2\le\cdots$ are the poles of $f$ ordered by increasing modulus.

Problem: Establish analogous asymptotic relations between the ordered eigenvalues $\varepsilon_j^{(n)}$ of the Hankel matrices $H_p^{(n)}$ and the poles of $f$ under hypotheses on $f$ that are weaker than membership in the Pick–Nevanlinna class. In particular, identify natural classes of meromorphic functions $f$ for which a formula of the type $\limsup_{n\to\infty}(\varepsilon_j^{(n)})^{1/n} = 1/|\lambda_j|$ (or a suitable variant) continues to hold.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for this question (asking what can be said about eigenvalues of Hankel matrices generated by Taylor coefficients of $f$ under hypotheses weaker than the Pick–Nevanlinna condition) did not turn up any specific resolution attributed to this problem. Related literature on Hankel pencil methods for pole recovery and on eigenvalue bounds for positive Hankel matrices exists, but no source found explicitly answers the posed problem.

status_evidence.title: Recovery of rational functions via Hankel pencil method and sensitivities of the poles
status_evidence.snippet: Poles of rational functions located inside and outside the unit circle can be reconstructed independently as eigenvalues of special Hankel matrix pencils.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats pole recovery via Hankel-pencil eigenvalues, but does not address the Pick–Nevanlinna eigenvalue/pole asymptotic in the weakened setting.

status_evidence.title: Positive Hankel Matrices, Eigenvalues and Total Positivity
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs intervals containing all eigenvalues of positive Hankel matrices.
status_evidence.claim: General eigenvalue localization is studied, but the specific asymptotic question is not resolved here.
